correctness.rationale: The source definition was read directly. For every large time n in a mixed hyperbolic Riesz splitting, one unit stable vector has image norm below 1/2 and one unit unstable vector has image norm above 2. The normalized segment joining them stays on the unit sphere and continuity forces an intermediate vector with image norm exactly 1, defeating any uniform cutoff. The pure stable and pure unstable cases follow from the spectral-radius formula. In finite dimension, a unit-circle eigenvalue supplies the remaining obstruction. The diagonal witness has exact closed-form unit vectors and its two defining identities were replayed by exact rational arithmetic.

originality.rationale: The inspected motivating preprint states the opposite implication and builds its claimed equivalences on it. Its proof applies valid stable- and unstable-subspace estimates to arbitrary mixed vectors without controlling cancellation/interpolation between the two sectors. Exact-term, alias, spectral, and mixed-dichotomy searches in the published finding index and web literature found no implication-equivalent correction. The closest own earlier result from the same source concerns asymptotic and strong asymptotic expansivity of normal operators and does not state or imply the super-asymptotic mixed-subspace obstruction.
residual_risks: An equivalent mixed stable/unstable obstruction may have appeared in older operator-dynamics literature under terminology unrelated to “super asymptotic expansivity”; no such statement was surfaced by the recorded alias searches.
Only version v1 of the motivating preprint was inspected; a later revision could independently repair the theorem. This does not affect the correctness of the claim relative to v1.

value.rationale: The result corrects the central equivalence advertised by a fresh paper introducing the super-asymptotic notion. It identifies the precise structural obstruction—simultaneous stable and unstable spectral sectors—gives an exact finite-dimensional classification, and supplies a two-dimensional surjective Hilbert-space counterexample. This changes several downstream statements in the motivating source and is substantially more informative than a numerical or isolated counterexample.
